html:
The Algerian War was the war for Algeria's independence from France, fought from November 1954 to March 1962. It was one of the bloodiest wars of decolonisation.

France had ruled Algeria since 1830 and treated it as part of France itself (French Algeria). About a million European settlers, the pieds-noirs, held most of the power and good land. After the massacres at Sétif and Guelma in 1945, nationalists turned to arms. On 1 November 1954 the National Liberation Front (FLN) launched attacks across the country.

  • Both sides used terror. French forces used torture, mass internment and the forced resettlement of villagers.
  • In 1957 French paratroopers broke the FLN in the city of Algiers, the fight shown in the film The Battle of Algiers.
  • In 1958 settlers and army officers in Algiers rose up, which brought down the French government and returned Charles de Gaulle to power.
  • De Gaulle moved toward self-determination. Settler extremists in the OAS answered with bombings, and generals tried a coup in 1961.

The Évian Accords brought a ceasefire on 19 March 1962, and Algeria became independent on 5 July. Most settlers left for France. Algerian deaths are put anywhere from a few hundred thousand to the 1.5 million claimed by Algeria. The FLN ruled as a single party, and the new state took over the oil and gas in the Sahara through Sonatrach. The writer Assia Djebar wrote of the war's women.
sum: The Algerian War was the war for Algeria's independence from France, fought from November 1954 to March 1962. It was one of the bloodiest wars of decolonisation.
